model: Regulated utility FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT revenue. The engine's 'revenue' line carries FY2026E ongoing net income to common: 9M-2026 ongoing EPS 3.37 x 629M diluted = 2,120 plus Q4 implied by the 4.10-4.16 guidance midpoint (0.76 x ~637M) = ~2,605. The 'ebitda margin' line carries FCFE as a percent of net income (dividends less net common issuance); D&A, capex, tax, SBC and working capital are zero because net income is already after all of them.
inputs.share_count_basis: 635.115M outstanding at 2026-09-30 (10-Q balance sheet) + 3.3M Q3 common-stock equivalents (treasury-method forwards and awards). Held FLAT: the 79.4M unsettled forward shares and all later plan issuance are charged as negative equity flows (proceeds deducted from FCFE), so growing the count as well would double-count the dilution.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt held at ZERO in the engine because the flow is post-interest FCFE discounted at the cost of equity; deducting debt again would count it twice. Actual at 2026-09-30: long-term debt 36,539 + current portion 999 + short-term debt 3,060 = 40,598 (excluding 1,277 finance leases), cash 2,483.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE: ~1,480 dividends paid less ~1,950 net common issuance (about 900 through 9M per APIC/par movement plus the 1,044 collared forward due Dec 2026). Not reported_fcf less SBC: on this route SBC is already inside net income.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 2026-09-30: OCF 5,077 less capex 12,693. Structurally negative in a capex supercycle and not a valuation input.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (57). Already expensed inside net income, so the projected SBC path is zero and house and street values coincide (band collapsed).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a COST OF EQUITY. USD flows, USD rate: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13 close) + regulated-utility beta ~0.6 x 4.75% ERP = ~8.0% base. Bull 7.5% (rates ease), bear 9.0% (long rates stay above 5% and wildfire/regulatory risk is repriced). Note SO was built the same week at 7.5%; XEL at 7.5% is roughly $10/share higher (see required_return_table).
inputs.lease_treatment: None needed: lease interest and amortisation are inside net income; lease liabilities are not deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest; all equity is common stockholders' equity.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity, the regulated-utility precedent set by SO (dcf-methods has no utility row; closest is the bank FCFE-at-CoE family). An unlevered owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here: TTM OCF 5.1bn against 12.7bn capex and a 70bn 2027-2031 plan make FCF structurally negative, and value is created by earning an allowed ROE (~9.3-10.5%) on a growing rate base, not by free cash. FLOW: net income to common less the increase in common equity needed to fund rate-base growth = dividends less net share issuance. Run through the Drivers engine with 'revenue' = ongoing net income and 'ebitda margin' = FCFE/net income; net debt zero. Years 1-5 are built bottom-up from the 10-Q financing plan (8.0bn equity 2027-2031, front-loaded by the 5.8bn of forwards maturing Dec 2026-Dec 2028) and the 4-6% dividend objective; years 6-10 use FCFE/NI = 1 - g/ROE as rate-base growth fades. The 1,044 collared forward maturing Dec 2026 falls between the valuation date and Y1 and is deducted in equity_bridge. Negative FCFE in 2027-2028 is real: equity raised exceeds dividends paid. CAVEAT: FY2026E base is guidance-derived, not a filed annual figure; 10-year yield is a single-source print. Entry price at the 15% house hurdle is far below any price a regulated utility trades at and should be read as 'never a 15% compounder', not as a target.

equity_bridge.item: 2025 collared forward equity settlement due Dec 2026 (15.1M shares)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q note 4 forward table; proceeds from new holders between valuation date and Y1, charged as a negative flow to existing holders

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: ongoing EPS (3.17 FY2022 -> 3.80 FY2025, 6.2%) cross-checked to the 6-8%+ long-term objective; NOT equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (10-12%) exceeds GAAP EPS CAGR (2.6-4.2%) by far more than 30%: equity is growing through share issuance (shares 550M FY2022 -> 635M Q3-2026), not retained earnings alone, and GAAP EPS is depressed by wildfire charges (Marshall 287 in FY2025). Book-value growth overstates per-share growth for a serial issuer.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue is pass-through fuel-driven and uninformative (FY2020 revenue missing from the DB, so no 5-year figure). FCF is negative in every year since FY2012; CAGRs undefined. Rate base 42.2bn FY2023 -> 55.8bn FY2025 (15% a year). Ongoing ROE 10.76% FY2022 -> 10.38% FY2025; PSCo earned only 5.66% in FY2025 on wildfire charges.

base.growth_note: Net income growth, not revenue. 2027 = guidance midpoint EPS 4.55 x ~660M average diluted shares = ~3,003; then EPS +8%, +8%, +7%, +6.5% on a share count rising ~3% a year from plan issuance. Consistent with rate base growing ~17/14/12/8/5% on the 16.3/14.7/15.2/13.1/10.8bn capex schedule and implied ROE on average equity of 10.6-10.8%. Years 6-10 fade to 3.5%.
base.margin_note: FCFE / net income. 2027-2031 = dividends (DPS +5% a year from 2.36, payout drifting 57% -> 50%) less issuance of 2,000 / 2,700 / 1,300 / 1,000 / 1,000 (= the 8.0bn plan). 2032+ = 1 - g/ROE at 10.4% ROE.
base.rationale: Management plan taken at face value on capex and financing, mid-range on EPS.

bull.growth_note: 2027 at the top of guidance (4.62); the ~10bn of 'line of sight' data-center capex is added to the base plan, EPS grows 9-10% through 2031.
bull.margin_note: Extra capex needs ~3bn more equity (750 a year 2028-2031) and dividends grow 6%; ROE 10.8% from 2032.
bull.rationale: Large-load upside converts to signed agreements; more growth, but more equity raised first.

bear.growth_note: Same capex and equity issuance as base (the equity need is set by capex, not earnings) but earned ROE compresses from 10.4% to ~9.5% by 2031 as rate cases settle below ask, as Colorado (9.3%) and New Mexico (9.5%) just did. EPS growth ~4-5%.
bear.margin_note: Dividend growth at the 4% floor; 2032+ = 1 - g/ROE at 9.5%.
bear.rationale: Affordability pushback plus a further wildfire event or adverse Texas AG outcome, with long rates staying above 5%.

scenario_narratives.base: The 70bn 2027-2031 base plan is executed and financed as disclosed (8.0bn equity, front-loaded through forwards already struck). Net income compounds ~12% a year to 2031 while the share count grows ~3% a year, giving 7-8% EPS growth off guidance midpoints, inside the 6-8%+ objective. Earned ROE holds near 10.5%. FCFE is negative in 2027-2028 because equity raised exceeds dividends, then turns positive as issuance tapers and rate-base growth fades toward 3.5% by 2036.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-center and large-load demand converts to contracts (Google Pine Island approved, further ESAs follow), adding roughly 10bn of capex under tariffs that keep it accretive. EPS grows 9-10%, earned ROE edges up to 10.8%, and lower long rates take the cost of equity to 7.5%. The upside is muted because the extra growth must be pre-funded with more equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulators lean on affordability: allowed and earned ROEs drift to ~9.5%, so the same capital programme and the same share issuance earn less. A new wildfire loss above the ~450m of insurance, or an adverse Texas Attorney General outcome on Smokehouse Creek, is absorbed in the lower earned return. Long rates stay above 5% and the cost of equity is 9.0%. The stock traded at this level ($47-56) in October 2023 and March 2024.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% and bull trimmed to 30%: two rate cases settled well below ask in the last quarter, wildfire exposure in Colorado and the Texas Panhandle is structural and under-insured, and the stock is a bond proxy with the 10-year above 5%. Bull is still weighted above bear because of the 21-year record of meeting guidance and the contracted nature of the large-load pipeline.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is worth the present value of what its equity holders receive net of what they are asked to put back in. Xcel earns about 10.4% on equity against a cost of equity near 8%, so growth creates value, but only on the spread, and during the 2027-2028 capex peak holders contribute more than they receive. Value is therefore dominated by the terminal (over 80%) and is highly sensitive to the cost of equity: each 50bp is roughly $10 a share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: 7.5% instead of 8.0% lifts base value by roughly 15%; the market price implies about 7.4%
Earned ROE: every 100bp of ROE compression is worth roughly a tenth of net income with no offsetting reduction in equity required
Equity issuance beyond the 8.0bn plan if incremental data-center capex is added or FFO/debt slips toward the 13% downgrade threshold
Wildfire: Smokehouse Creek losses of 475-525m with the upper bound not estimable and the Texas AG suit open; insurance cover ~450m per event
Terminal payout: year-10 FCFE/NI of 66% is capitalised; a steady state at 3% growth would support ~71%, so the terminal is modestly conservative
FY2026E base and 2027 Y1 rest on guidance (4.10-4.16 and 4.48-4.62), both assuming constructive outcomes in all pending rate cases
